result.title: Dynamical Kernel Attention: Estimating the Present from a Record of the Past
result.summary: Standard self-attention compares tokens by similarity but does not account for how much of a past state survives to the present. We introduce Dynamical Kernel Attention (DKA), which derives attention from robust estimation of a latent state evolving under stochastic dynamics. As a past state decays toward equilibrium under the dynamics, the information it carries about the present vanishes, bounding the total evidence a head can draw. Unlike recency biases, DKA can abstain when relevant evidence is weak and guarantees a bounded error when old tokens are discarded. DKA preserves the parallel structure and computational cost of standard attention. We present the model and its theory; empirical evaluation is deferred to a subsequent version.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Dynamical Kernel Attention：把注意力视作对随机动态下演化的 latent state 的稳健估计，使过去状态携带的关于当前的信息随衰减而受限，并可在相关证据薄弱时弃权；方法保持标准注意力的并行结构与计算成本，目前只给出模型与理论，实验留待后续版本。
AI.relevance_reason: 「旧 token 证据衰减有界、证据不足即弃权」这一机制可能对应 LVR 中 STOP 决策与视觉证据筛选／缓存遗忘的收益成本问题，可供核查；但论文目前仅停留在理论层面、未含多模态验证，迁移效果需自行判断。
